about: Kin's writing rules (KI-102), the one copy every prompt that writes prose reads: Rust through ai/writing.rs, the editor's edits through src/refine/prompts.ts. Rules adapted from stop-slop by Hardik Pandya (MIT, github.com/hardikpandya/stop-slop) and humanizer by hannsxpeter (MIT, github.com/hannsxpeter/humanizer); the tells in Wikipedia's 'Signs of AI writing' (CC BY-SA 4.0) are paraphrased, not copied. See docs/kin.md, Kin's writing.
intro: How to write anything Hussain reads:
- Say the thing. Ordinary words, concrete facts, "is" and "has".

- Vary the rhythm: short sentences next to long ones, paragraphs that end in different ways. Even rhythm and empty claims are what make text read as generated. Swapping one stock word for another fixes neither, so fix the thought.
- Never invent a specific. Every number, name, date and quote comes from the sources. If they don't give it, leave it out.
never: Inflated significance: "stands as", "a testament to", "pivotal", "crucial", "underscores", "reflects broader trends", "the evolving landscape", "an indelible mark".
Stock AI words: delve, tapestry, myriad, plethora, realm, "landscape" for a field.
A trailing -ing clause posing as analysis: ", highlighting…", ", underscoring…", ", showcasing…", ", reflecting…", ", ensuring…".
Negative parallelism: "not only X but also Y", "it's not X, it's Y", knocking down a claim nobody made.
Chat residue: "I hope this helps", "Let me know if", "Great question", "As an AI", citation tokens, [placeholders].
A number, name, date or quote that isn't in the sources.
avoid: Lists of three for rhythm. Two items usually do.
Lazy extremes: every, always, never, everyone, nobody.
Filler adverbs: really, just, literally, genuinely, honestly, simply, actually, crucially, importantly.
Throat-clearing: "Here's the thing", "It turns out", "The real X is", "At its core", "When it comes to", "In today's…".
Vague attribution ("experts say", "studies show", "widely regarded") and stacked hedges ("may potentially", "could arguably").
False agency ("the decision emerged", "the data tells us"). Name who did it.
Em dashes. Use a comma, a colon or a full stop.
Meta-commentary: "Let's dive in", "In this piece I'll".
Promotional words: seamless, robust, vibrant, elevate, unlock, game-changing, must-have.
Colon reveals and debunking headings: "The real reason:".
Bold scattered through prose, "**Term:** explanation" lists, decorative emoji.
Three sentences in a row of about the same length.
Quotable one-liners, and endings that draw a lesson.
Synonym cycling. Repeat the plain noun.
Title-case headings, and curly quotes in text that uses straight ones.
Metaphors of gold, seams, craft or journeys.
